exercise.name: Barbell Deadlift from Deficit

reference.title: Barbell Deadlift from Deficit
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be read from this environment, gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy, so the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

exercise.bodyPart: Hips (glutes) and back of the thighs

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace before the bar leaves the floor, hold through the pull, breathe out at the top or once the plates are back down.
breathing.cadence: About 1.9 s up, a short lockout, about 2 s down, reset on the floor

prescription.tempo: Controlled pull from the floor, short lockout, controlled lowering
prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen: usually 10-20 % lighter than your floor deadlift; keep the back flat off the floor, about 2-3 reps in reserve.
prescription.progression: Add 2.5-5 kg when every rep leaves the floor with a flat back; or raise the platform a little (2.5 to 10 cm).

cues.text: Stand on the platform, bar over mid-foot, plates on the floor in front. Hinge down and grip just outside the knees, shins to the bar, hips a little lower than in a floor deadlift, back flat, brace.
Push the platform away: the bar slides up the shins, hips and shoulders rising together, then drive the hips through once the bar passes the knees.
Stand tall, hips and knees straight, shoulders over the bar.
Hips back first, bar close to the thighs, then bend the knees to set the plates down on the floor.
Plates touch down softly; keep the brace or take a new breath, then pull again.

mistakes.mistake: Back rounding in the deeper start
mistakes.fix: Use a lower platform or a lighter load until the back stays flat off the floor.
Push with the legs so the hips and shoulders rise together.
Keep the bar against the shins and thighs, lats tight.
2.5-10 cm is enough; more turns it into a different lift.

kinematics.norm: More knee bend at the start than a floor deadlift because the bar starts lower relative to the feet (clinical opinion); conventional deadlift about 65-85 degrees (Swinton 2011)
Hips above the knees, below the shoulders, deeper than from the floor (clinical opinion; conventional start: Escamilla 2002)
Trunk more inclined than in a floor deadlift at the start (clinical opinion)
Controlled lift and lowering; reset on the floor each rep (clinical opinion)

cautions: Only add the deficit once the floor deadlift is solid; the deeper start asks more of the hips and hamstrings.
The platform must be solid and not slide; leave the plates clear of it.
Low-back pain: go back to the floor or to blocks.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Tight hips or hamstrings: lower platform (2.5-5 cm).
Grip: chalk or straps for top sets.

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Main hip extensor through the longer pull (Escamilla 2002).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Main hip extensor through the longer pull (Escamilla 2002).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Extend the hip from the deeper hinge (Lee 2018).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Extend the hip from the deeper hinge (Lee 2018).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Straighten the knees through the extra range off the floor.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Straighten the knees through the extra range off the floor.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the back flat with the bar hanging in front (Escamilla 2002).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the back flat with the bar hanging in front (Escamilla 2002).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Adductor magnus assists hip extension from the bottom.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Adductor magnus assists hip extension from the bottom.
muscleNotes.lats_r: Keep the bar close to the legs.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Keep the bar close to the legs.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Hold the shoulders against the bar.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Hold the shoulders against the bar.
muscleNotes.calves_r: Keep the feet flat on the platform.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Keep the feet flat on the platform.
